outcome: Since 26 January 2024 nothing has settled or moved either part of this problem: no infinite family of strongly regular geodetic graphs and no strongly regular geodetic graph that is not a Moore graph has been reported. The window events all concern the hypothetical degree-57 Moore graph, parameters (3250,57,0,1): a 2024 Symmetry paper and a 2026 Axioms paper by Smith and Montemanni (partial and negative results on constructions, not a graph), and a June 2026 arXiv preprint by Ishida (a conditional restriction on automorphisms). The degree-57 case is still open, and the 2020 Makhnev nonexistence claim it touches is disputed and unpublished as far as I could find.
problem_asks: Part (a): whether there exist infinitely many strongly regular geodetic graphs. Part (b): whether there exists any strongly regular geodetic graph that is not a Moore graph. Unpacked: 'strongly regular' means parameters (v,k,λ,μ) with each adjacent pair having λ common neighbours and each non-adjacent pair μ common neighbours; 'geodetic' means every pair of vertices is joined by exactly one shortest path. 'Moore graph' is read as the diameter-2 Moore graphs, i.e. the strongly regular graphs with λ=0 and μ=1 (C5 = (5,2,0,1), Petersen = (10,3,0,1), Hoffman-Singleton = (50,7,0,1), and the hypothetical (3250,57,0,1)). So part (b) asks for a strongly regular geodetic graph with λ≥1. Two readings I have adopted, both from the definitions and the Wikipedia trichotomy (see summary): (1) a non-complete strongly regular graph is geodetic exactly when μ=1, so the class in question is the strongly regular graphs with μ=1; (2) complete graphs are excluded from the bullet, since they have no non-adjacent pairs and the bullet's examples are all diameter 2.

events.what_happened: A. J. Hoffman and R. R. Singleton, 'On Moore graphs with diameters 2 and 3', IBM Journal of Research and Development (1960). For diameter 2 the degree must be 2, 3, 7 or 57; degree 57 would force order 57²+1 = 3250. Degrees 2, 3 and 7 give the 5-cycle, the Petersen graph and the Hoffman-Singleton graph; the degree-57 case was left undecided. Read via the Wikipedia 'Moore graph' article (opened, which says the degree-57 graph's existence 'is unknown and is one of the most famous open problems in graph theory'); the 1960 paper itself was not opened (a copy was listed in search results).
events.delivers: Restricts diameter-2 Moore graphs (the λ=0 strongly regular geodetic graphs) to degrees 2, 3, 7 and 57, and establishes the existence of the graphs for degrees 2, 3, 7. Establishes nothing about λ≥1 and nothing about infinitude.
events.remains: Both parts (a) and (b): no non-Moore graph and no infinite family. The degree-57 Moore case is left open.
events.directly_checkable: The 5-cycle, Petersen and Hoffman-Singleton graphs are small graphs that can be checked by hand; I did not check them. Uniqueness for degree 7 is classical, and a search summary mentions an Elkies outline and a 1974 James proof; neither was opened.
events.direction: Cuts toward existence for degrees 2, 3 and 7, all of which are Moore graphs, and leaves degree 57 open. It has no bearing on a non-Moore graph or on infinitude.
events.object: The three existing diameter-2 Moore graphs: the 5-cycle, SRG(5,2,0,1); the Petersen graph, SRG(10,3,0,1); and the Hoffman-Singleton graph, SRG(50,7,0,1). All have λ=0, so they are Moore graphs and not non-Moore examples. The degree-57 case would be an SRG(3250,57,0,1); no such graph is exhibited and none has been proved not to exist.

events.what_happened: J. G. Stemple, 'Geodetic graphs of diameter two', Journal of Combinatorial Theory Series B (1974), as cited in search summaries of the Blokhuis-Brouwer and Scapellato references; the paper was not opened. Stemple's 1966 Yale dissertation, 'A Further Characterization of Geodetic Graphs', is also cited in search summaries. The structural result as reported by the Wikipedia 'Geodetic graph' article (opened): every geodetic graph of diameter two is one of three types: a block graph whose maximal cliques all share one vertex, a strongly regular graph with μ=1, or a graph with exactly two vertex degrees.
events.delivers: Structural trichotomy for diameter-2 geodetic graphs. My reading: a non-complete regular geodetic graph has diameter 2 and so is a strongly regular graph with μ=1, because the other two classes are not regular. Together with the fact that every strongly regular graph with μ=1 is geodetic, this identifies the bullet's class with the strongly regular graphs with μ=1. It does not decide whether that class is infinite, or whether it contains a member with λ≥1.
events.doubts: The trichotomy is taken from the Wikipedia summary and from search summaries of later papers; the original theorem was not read. The reduction to μ=1 is my reading of it, not a stated result in any source I opened.
events.direction: Structural; it cuts neither toward existence nor toward nonexistence.

events.what_happened: A. Blokhuis and A. E. Brouwer, 'Geodetic graphs of diameter two', Geometriae Dedicata 25 (1-3) (1988), 527-533, DOI 10.1007/BF00191941. Per a search summary of the TU/e research portal, the abstract says the paper surveys what is known about geodetic graphs of diameter two and 'discuss[es] the implications of a new strong necessary condition for the existence of such graphs'. Wikipedia cites it for the open existence question about strongly regular geodetic graphs. Not opened.
events.delivers: Not established by this record. The necessary condition it states was not read, so whether it bears on strongly regular μ=1 graphs with λ≥1 is unknown here.
events.remains: Not established by this record; potentially both parts (a) and (b).
events.direction: Unknown; the content was not read.

events.what_happened: J. Deutsch and P. H. Fisher (spelled 'Fischer' in some search summaries), 'On strongly regular graphs with μ=1', European Journal of Combinatorics 22(3) (2001), 303-306, DOI 10.1006/eujc.2000.0472. Volume, pages and DOI are confirmed by two search summaries; the paper was not opened. The result is quoted second-hand in Elder, Piggott, Stober, Thumm and Weiß, 'Finite groups with geodetic Cayley graphs' (arXiv 2406.00261; abstract opened, body not readable): if a strongly regular graph with μ=1 has λ>0, then λ>1 and either (δ,λ)=(21,2) or δ≥(λ+1)(λ+13).
events.delivers: A parameter restriction on the non-Moore case, as quoted: a strongly regular μ=1 graph with λ≥1 has λ≥2 and either (k,λ)=(21,2) or k≥(λ+1)(λ+13). It restricts parameters only. It produces no graph and decides neither part of the problem.
events.remains: Part (b) for every admissible parameter set not excluded by the restriction, and part (a), infinitude.

events.what_happened: A. A. Makhnev, 'Moore graph with parameters (3250,57,0,1) does not exist', arXiv:2010.13443, math.CO, Russian text with English abstract. v1 26 October 2020; v2 9 November 2020 (abstract page opened). The paper claims to prove that a distance-regular graph with intersection array {55,54,2;1,1,54} does not exist, and as a corollary that no Moore graph of degree 57 exists. It relies on the Jurišić-Vidali equivalence (a Moore graph of degree k>3 exists iff a distance-regular graph with array {k-2,k-3,2;1,1,k-3} exists), as stated in the abstract. No journal publication was found in any search. Makhnev's other 2020 work, in Algebra i logika, is on a different topic (a distance-regular graph with that array), per a search summary.
events.delivers: If correct, a nonexistence result for one Moore case: no Moore graph of diameter 2 and degree 57. It removes a λ=0 candidate only. It establishes nothing about strongly regular geodetic graphs with λ≥1, and nothing about infinitude.
events.remains: Both parts (a) and (b). The arXiv abstract mentions no non-Moore graph and no family.

events.what_happened: V. Faber and J. Keegan, 'Existence of a Moore graph of degree 57 is still open', arXiv:2210.09577, math.CO. Abstract page opened: v1 18 October 2022; v2 21 October 2022; v3 22 November 2022; v4 6 December 2022; v5 5 February 2023; v6 27 February 2023. Abstract, as read: the 2020 claim 'seems not to be correct'; they argue the proof's system of equations does not yield a contradiction, and propose an alternative family of permutation systems, such that 'the Moore graph exists if and only if there is a member of the family with no solutions'. The PDF was not readable through the tool; the detail that the system factors into small diagonal blocks each of which has solutions comes from a search summary and is not verified here. No journal reference is listed.
events.delivers: Moore-only. Disputes the 2020 nonexistence argument and reformulates existence of the degree-57 graph as the existence of a member of a permutation-system family with no solutions. It establishes neither existence nor nonexistence.
events.remains: Both parts (a) and (b). Existence of the degree-57 Moore graph is itself left open.

events.direction: Neutral on existence: it undermines a nonexistence argument and leaves existence open. Moore-only.

Montemanni, 'The missing Moore graph as an optimization problem', EURO Journal on Computational Optimization (vol. 11, January 2023 per the DOAJ listing; DOAJ page returned HTTP 403, so the abstract is known only from a search snippet). events.what_happened: F. Stober and A. Weiß, 'Geodetic Graphs: Experiments and New Constructions', arXiv:2308.08970, math.CO/cs.DM. v1 17 August 2023; v2 27 January 2025 (opened, abstract and HTML v2). The enumeration program finds all geodetic graphs on at most 25 vertices and all regular geodetic graphs on at most 32 vertices. The regular search found only previously known graphs: odd cycles, complete graphs, the Petersen graph, and one cubic 'block of order 28' cited to Bosák. The paper also reports two new infinite families of geodetic graphs: H(m,n,p,s), built by gluing graphs along cliques, with diameter 3s+4; and F_k (k odd, at least 3), built from two copies of C_k plus extra vertices and having degrees 2 and 3. The paper does not state a general vertex count for F_k; the 2k+13 figure is a reader's derivation from the construction. v2 corrects v1's count of 32 to 33 biconnected geodetic graphs on 25 vertices. A MathWorld search summary gives a journal version, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 33 (2026), P3.64, DOI 10.37236/13950; I did not verify this at the journal.
events.revisions: v1 17 Aug 2023 (count of 25-vertex biconnected geodetic graphs given as 32); v2 27 Jan 2025 (corrected to 33). Journal version reported as EJC 33 (2026) P3.64, unverified.
events.delivers: A finite result: among regular geodetic graphs on at most 32 vertices, there is no strongly regular geodetic graph other than the Petersen graph, and the odd cycles and complete graphs. The two new infinite families are not strongly regular: H has diameter at least 4, and F_k is not regular. This settles no infinitude question, and says nothing about strongly regular geodetic graphs on more than 32 vertices.
events.remains: Part (a), infinitude. Part (b) for strongly regular μ=1 graphs with λ≥1 on more than 32 vertices. The Hoffman-Singleton graph (50 vertices) lies outside the search range.
events.directly_checkable: The 28-vertex cubic graph and F_k are explicit constructions, but I did not check either.
events.doubts: The first version had a counting error (32 against 33). Two inferences are mine, not stated in the paper: a regular geodetic graph of diameter 2 must be strongly regular with μ=1, so the cubic 28-vertex graph (not strongly regular with μ=1 on 28 vertices, since the only cubic such graph is the Petersen graph) must have diameter at least 3; and the search's 'biconnected' qualifier leaves open whether a non-biconnected strongly regular μ=1 graph would be covered.
events.direction: Cuts neither toward existence nor toward nonexistence of a non-Moore graph beyond the range it searched; within that range, no non-Moore strongly regular geodetic graph appears.
events.object: Two infinite families of geodetic graphs, neither strongly regular: H(m,n,p,s), built from graphs h(m,n,s), h(n,p,s), h(p,m,s) joined by identifying cliques, of diameter 3s+4 for m,n,p≥2, s≥0; and F_k, built from two copies of the k-cycle plus a few extra vertices, with degrees 2 and 3. Both are explicit constructions, not existence proofs.

ai.disclosed_cost: 16 days of computation across the enumeration, with about 15 days spent on n=25 using 24 threads (per the arXiv text as summarised).

events.what_happened: Y. Ishida, 'No involutions in the missing Moore graph', arXiv:2606.29183, math.CO. Abstract page opened: v1 submitted 28 June 2026; v2 8 July 2026. Claim: if a Moore graph of diameter 2 and degree 57 exists, it has no involutory automorphisms, so its automorphism group has odd order. The method is a trace-rank identity for finite graphs, obtained from Brauer quotients of p-permutation lattices, applied to the eigenvalue -8 summand over the 2-adic integers. The abstract does not claim existence or nonexistence. The PDF returned binary through the tool and could not be read; the abstract page is the only text read. The abstract mentions no AI system.

disputes.summary: Makhnev (arXiv 2010.13443, 2020) claims that the degree-57 Moore graph does not exist. Faber and Keegan (arXiv 2210.09577, 2022-23) say the argument does not reach a contradiction and that the claim 'seems not to be correct'. No refereed resolution found. summary: Found: no event since January 2024 that touches the two parts of the bullet. Infinitude is not decided and no non-Moore strongly regular geodetic graph is known. The bullet's own source (Wikipedia 'Geodetic graph', opened, last revised 26 December 2025) lists C5, Petersen and Hoffman-Singleton as the known strongly regular geodetic graphs, says it is not known whether there are more or infinitely many, and asks the question as an open problem. Structure I relied on: every strongly regular graph with μ=1 is geodetic of diameter 2; the Wikipedia trichotomy for diameter-2 geodetic graphs (block graphs, strongly regular μ=1, or two-degree graphs) then makes the non-complete strongly regular geodetic graphs exactly the strongly regular graphs with μ=1, and λ=0 gives the Moore graphs. A search summary attributes to a survey the open problem of whether there are only finitely many strongly regular graphs with μ=1; I could not open that survey, so I record it unverified. Parameter restrictions for λ≥1 come from Deutsch-Fischer (2001), quoted second-hand, and Bagchi (2006), read in abstract: λ≥1 forces k≥(λ+1)(λ+2) and, per Deutsch-Fischer, either (k,λ)=(21,2) or k≥(λ+1)(λ+13). These narrow the search but produce no example. Within the window, the only events are about the degree-57 Moore graph: Smith and Montemanni (Symmetry, November 2024: 20 potential subgraphs against 15 known, under a cyclic-group assumption with CP-SAT; Axioms, May 2026: the summaries disagree on whether it is positive or negative for construction, with the title suggesting a construction and at least one summary saying a cyclic-group construction is impossible), and Ishida (arXiv June 2026: no involutory automorphisms if such a graph exists). Those concern only λ=0 and say nothing about part (a) or part (b). Earlier: Makhnev (October 2020) claims the degree-57 graph does not exist; Faber and Keegan (October 2022) dispute the argument. Stober and Weiß (August 2023, revised January 2025) enumerated geodetic graphs up to 25 vertices and regular geodetic graphs up to 32, finding no non-Moore strongly regular geodetic graph in that range, and their two new infinite families are not strongly regular. Two points are close. First, the 28-vertex cubic graph in Stober-Weiß is not strongly regular with μ=1, so by the trichotomy it must have diameter at least 3; I am reasoning from the trichotomy here, not quoting the paper. Second, the Makhnev claim is not published as far as I could find, and the search returned an unexplained Epoch AI page with an access date of 12 October 2026, which is after today's date (11 October 2026); I have not relied on that page for anything except its description of the problem as unsolved with no recorded submission. AI: no source I opened credits an AI system with any result on this problem, nor reports an AI attempt. The Epoch FrontierMath open-problems page poses the degree-57 Moore graph as a benchmark task and records no solution. Neighbouring AI items that I found and judged not to bear on the bullet are listed under dead_ends. Smith and Montemanni's computations use the CP-SAT constraint solver, which I classify as a solver, not an AI system, under §5.4.
competing_reading: A reader could treat the degree-57 Moore graph as part of this problem, on the grounds that the bullet's 'strongly regular geodetic graphs' include it, so an existence or nonexistence result there changes the count of known strongly regular geodetic graphs. On the bullet's own wording, though, the question asks for infinitude and for a non-Moore member, and a resolved degree-57 case answers neither. A second reading treats the Makhnev nonexistence claim (2020) as established, which would close one Moore case and leave the bullet unchanged. A third reading takes Smith and Montemanni's 2026 Axioms title, 'The Moore Graph of Diameter 2 and Degree 57 via Cyclic Derangements', as evidence of a construction. Even if that were true it would be a Moore graph, which the bullet excludes. The strongest case for reading the window as containing a relevant event is that Ishida's and Smith-Montemanni's work restricts the same hypothetical graph that a non-Moore question would be tested against. It does not, since they restrict λ=0 only.
what_would_settle_it: For part (b): an explicit strongly regular graph with μ=1 and λ≥1, or a theorem excluding every admissible parameter set (k,λ) with λ≥1, which would need a sharper result than Deutsch-Fischer (2001) and Bagchi (2006). For part (a): a construction of infinitely many strongly regular μ=1 graphs, or a theorem bounding their number. Source-wise, I need: the full texts of Deutsch-Fischer (2001), Blokhuis-Brouwer (1988), Belousov-Makhnev (2006, venue unconfirmed) and Stemple (1974); the body of Elder et al. (2024) to check the quoted Deutsch-Fischer statement; Brouwer's strongly regular parameter tables, to see whether any μ=1 family with λ≥1 is listed; the Smith-Montemanni 2026 Axioms paper, to settle whether its title or its summary is right; Ishida (2026), readable in full; and a journal publication or independent check of Makhnev (2020). None of these would be needed to settle the Moore-only events, which bear only on the degree-57 graph.

events.credibility_reason: Author's erratum invalidates Theorem 3.1 and several dependent theorems; corrected statements stand.
Faber and Keegan dispute the key step (the system of equations yields no contradiction); unpublished after six years and later literature still calls the degree-57 case open.

judgement.why: The statement asks two things: whether infinitely many strongly regular geodetic graphs exist, and whether any non-Moore one exists. Every degree-57 Moore event (Makhnev, Faber-Keegan, Renteln, Dalfó, Mačaj-Širáň, Smith-Montemanni, Ishida) concerns only a Moore case. Settling it either way would add or remove at most one graph, so it answers neither part; I scored all of them none. Hoffman-Singleton 1960 shows that Moore graphs exist, which is not what either part asks, so it is none too. The Deutsch-Fischer and Bagchi parameter restrictions on the λ≥1 case narrow where a non-Moore example could be. They do not move a quantity that the statement asks about, so I scored them none and not bound; this was the closest call, and the outcome is the same either way because the events are pre-snapshot and would not tier as resolved. Stober-Weiß is a finite enumeration, so instances. Elder et al. is about Cayley graphs, so variant. No AI system is credited anywhere; CP-SAT is a solver.
judgement.doubts: The reading that μ=1 characterises the class rests on the researcher's inference from a Wikipedia summary of Stemple. The record says the Smith-Montemanni 2026 summaries disagree on whether it is positive or negative, but it is Moore-only either way. Journal verification for the published items was taken as digestion without seeing reports; it does not affect the outcome.
